newsitem.title: JAPAN: Idemitsu Petchem to cut naphtha imports by 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Idemitsu Petchem to cut naphtha imports by 10 pct.

text.p: Idemitsu Petrochemical Co Ltd said on Friday it plans to cut its naphtha imports by 10 percent starting in January amid dwindling profit margins caused by skyrocketing naphtha prices.
A company spokesman said the persistently high naphtha prices made such a move inevitable.
Naphtha is used as feedstock to manufacture petrochemical products such as ethylene and propylene.
Idemitsu Petrochemical, with an annual ethylene output capacity of 810,000 tonnes, procures around 3.5 million tonnes of naphtha per year, 65 percent of which are import cargoes.
The firm's total naphtha purchases are expected to fall by six to seven percent as a result of the import cut, he said.

Earlier this week, Mitsubishi Chemical Corp, the largest petrochemical firm in Japan, said it would cut its naphtha imports by 10 percent starting in January. Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd has also said it is considering reducing naphtha purchases in an effort to counter high naphtha prices.

Near-term naphtha prices on Asia's benchmark open-spec forward contract jumped more than 30 percent in the second half of 1996 due to high global crude oil prices as well as prospects for brisk regional demand for 1997.
